home.title: Deadlock+ | Discord Rich Presence and Stats for Deadlock
home.description: Deadlock+ is a free companion app for Deadlock: Discord Rich Presence, a server picker, a build editor, match history, rank and stats. No account needed.

free.title: Free, no account
free.body: Deadlock+ is free. There is nothing to sign up for.

local.title: Stays on your PC
local.body: Everything runs on your PC. The few things the app sends out are listed on the privacy page.

open.title: Nothing hidden
open.body: The app's code is public. Anyone can read it and see exactly what it does.

home.ready_body: Deadlock+ is free. Updates install only when you click, and each one is checked before it runs.

features.title: Rich Presence, Server Picker, Match History | Deadlock+
features.description: Everything Deadlock+ does for Deadlock: Discord Rich Presence, a server picker, live match info, a build editor, match history, stats, replays and performance.
features.heading: Deadlock+ features
features.subtitle: Each page of Deadlock+ does one job. Here is what each one is for.

match.name: Around the match
match.blurb: Show friends what you are playing, pick where you play and follow your match as it happens.

builds.name: Item builds
builds.blurb: Find a build for your hero, then make it your own.

progress.name: Your progress
progress.blurb: See how you are doing, match by match and over time.

upkeep.name: Upkeep
upkeep.blurb: The chores around the game, in one place.

discord_presence.name: Discord Rich Presence
discord_presence.summary: Show what you are playing on your Discord profile.

points.1: Detailed shows your hero, mode and match timer. Basic shows only that you are in Deadlock.
points.2: Your hero icon is the big image, and your rank badge the small one in ranked matches.
points.3: Change the text, images and timer Discord shows for each activity.
points.4: Off until you turn it on in the Presence page, where you also pick which Discord apps show it.

server_picker.name: Server Picker
server_picker.summary: Pick which server regions you play on.

points.1: Block the regions you do not want, and unblock them later.
points.2: See your ping to every region before you choose.
points.3: Bring over your blocked regions from ServerPickerX and CS2ServerPicker.

live.name: Live
live.summary: Both teams in your current match, with the server and your ping.

points.1: A scoreboard for both teams: rank, souls, kills, deaths, assists and damage.
points.2: The server you are on and your ping while you play.
points.3: Follows the game from queue to results, which land in your match history.

builds.name: Builds
builds.summary: Public builds for any hero, starting with the one you played last.

points.1: This week's favourites come first. Filter by hero, tag, language, author and name.
points.2: A build shows its win rate once it has enough recent matches.
points.3: Open a build to see its shop and ability order as the game draws them.
points.4: Hover an item or ability for the game's tooltip, with your stats at that point in the build.
points.5: Favourite a public build and it shows in the Mine tab and in your favourites in the game.
points.6: Copy for game and Paste code move builds between Deadlock+ and the game's Create New Build.

build_editor.name: Build editor
build_editor.summary: Edit any build, yours or a public one, on a copy of the game's shop page.

points.1: Drag items in from the shop and drag a category's edges to resize it.
points.2: Sizes snap so categories look the same at 1080p, 1440p, 4K and in the Build Browser.
points.3: A souls timeline shows when each item and ability step becomes affordable.
points.4: Click abilities to set the ability order. Orders the game would reject are blocked.
points.5: Undo and redo every change, and restore any of the last 20 saved versions.
points.6: Saves go to your game files, with a backup of the file before every write.

match_history.name: Match History
match_history.summary: Every match on record for your account, grouped into play sessions.

points.1: Each session shows its verdict, record and rank change above its matches.
points.2: Plain notes on when you play best.
points.3: A break reminder notification after three losses in a row, if you turn it on.
points.4: Filter by mode, hero, outcome and date.
points.5: Open a match for the full scoreboard: both teams, items, ranks and bans.
points.6: Souls and damage over time, when items were bought, objectives and accolades.

stats.name: Stats
stats.summary: Your rank, and your results over the last 7, 30 or 90 days or all time.

points.1: Progress to the next rank and your demotion shields.
points.2: What your next win or loss is worth.
points.3: An outlook: the winrate that holds your rank, next to your recent one.
points.4: Your rank over time, with each promotion and demotion marked.
points.5: Win rate, streaks, playtime and numbers for each hero.
points.6: How close you are to qualifying for the leaderboard.

mutes.name: Mutes
mutes.summary: Manage the players you have muted.

points.1: View, add, unmute, export and import muted players.
points.2: A backup is made before every change.
Pin the ones to keep and clean up the rest.

storage.name: Storage
storage.summary: See how much space the game takes on your drive.

points.1: How much space Deadlock and Deadlock+ each use.
points.2: Clear files the game makes again on its own.

performance.name: Performance
performance.summary: Measure how smoothly the game runs, then compare.

points.1: Record a play session: FPS, your lowest dips and stutters.
points.2: Check your installed mods for things that can slow the game down.
points.3: Compare two recordings side by side.

background.name: Background options
background.summary: Runs quietly until you need it.

points.1: Start with Windows and stay in the tray, by the clock.
points.2: A reminder before Steam's weekly maintenance.
points.3: Turn on alerts for patches and news.

faq.title: Deadlock+ FAQ: Discord, Servers, Linux, Privacy
faq.description: Answers about Deadlock+: showing your match and rank on Discord, picking servers, Linux and Mac, where stats come from, privacy and open source.
faq.heading: Deadlock+ FAQ
faq.subtitle: Short answers to what people ask most.

free.question: Is Deadlock+ free? Do I need an account?
free.answer: Yes, it is free. There is no account to make and nothing to sign up for.

discord.question: How do I show my Deadlock match and rank on Discord?
discord.answer: Turn on Discord Rich Presence in the app's Presence page. Your Discord profile then shows your hero, mode and match timer, and your rank badge in ranked matches. You can change the text, images and timer Discord shows.

servers.question: How do I pick which servers I play on?
servers.answer: Open the Server Picker and block the regions you do not want. It shows your ping to every region first. On Windows it uses firewall rules, which is why the app asks for administrator rights. You can unblock a region at any time, and bring over your blocked regions from ServerPickerX or CS2ServerPicker.

platforms.question: Does it work on Linux? On Mac?
platforms.answer: Linux: yes, as a .deb or an AppImage. Support is best-effort, and some features need extra setup. Mac: no, macOS is not supported.

stats.question: Where do my stats and match history come from?
stats.answer: From the Deadlock API, a free community database. To fetch your matches and rank, the app sends it your Steam account ID and nothing else about you.

privacy.question: What does Deadlock+ record about me?
privacy.answer: The app runs on your PC. The few things it sends are listed one by one on GitHub, and anonymous usage data and error reports can be turned off in Settings. This website uses no cookies.

performance.question: Does it slow down the game?
performance.answer: We cannot guarantee it, but we try our best to keep Deadlock+'s resource use as low as possible.

open_source.question: Is Deadlock+ open source?
open_source.answer: Yes. The code is public on GitHub under GPL-3.0-or-later, so anyone can check what it does. What it costs to run and how many people use it are on the Transparency page.

smartscreen.title: Windows says it "protected your PC"?
smartscreen.body: Windows shows this blue screen for any app that few people have installed yet. It does not mean that something is wrong with the file. To carry on:
